article.Citation/Title: Johnson, M. W., Garcia-Romeu, A., Cosimano, M. P., & Griffiths, R. R. (2014). Pilot study of the 5-HT2AR agonist psilocybin in the treatment of tobacco addiction. Journal of Psychopharmacology, 28(11), 983-992.
article.Outcome: 12/15 (80%) biologically verified 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence at 6-month follow-up
article.InterventionDescription: Oral psilocybin, moderate (20mg/70kg, week 5) and high (30mg/70kg, weeks 7 and optionally 13) doses, within 15-week CBT-based smoking-cessation protocol with preparation, integration, and support meetings.

ae_events.Description: Challenging psychological experience during sessions - extreme (1 participant) or strong (5 participants) fear, fear of insanity, or feeling trapped in 6/15 participants; managed by staff, resolved by session end.
Transient increases in blood pressure and heart rate during psilocybin sessions (peak systolic 153 vs baseline 125 mmHg; peak HR 87 vs baseline 68 bpm); no intervention required.
Post-psilocybin headache in 8 of 10 participants assessed, mean duration 5.8 hours, onset ~6.2 hours post-dose, mean severity mild (2.6/6); 5 used OTC medication that evening.

article.Outcome: No single field-labeled 'primary outcome' appears in Methods. The Abstract leads with the SUD-behavioral finding: 'Biomarkers assessing smoking status, and self-report measures of smoking behavior demonstrated that 12 of 15 participants (80%) showed seven-day point prevalence abstinence at 6-month follow-up,' repeated verbatim in Results ('Based on the Timeline Follow-back and verified by CO and cotinine measures, 12 of 15 (80%) participants showed seven-day point prevalence abstinence at 6-month follow-up'). Selected per precedence rule (2) - the SUD-behavioral outcome the abstract leads with - over the paired t-tests reported later in Results for continuous cigarettes/day (t14=11.1, P<.001), breath CO (t14=3.8, P<.01), and urine cotinine (t14=2.3, P=.04), which are supporting analyses of the same underlying abstinence construct rather than the headline finding.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic accompanies the 12/15 (80%) abstinence rate; it is reported as a raw single-arm proportion with no comparator. The paired t-test statistics elsewhere in Results (t14=11.1 for TLFB cigarettes/day; t14=3.8 for CO; t14=2.3 for cotinine) are paired with the continuous pre/post smoking-reduction analyses, not with the abstinence-rate Outcome selected above, so they are not repurposed here.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 'Fifteen participants (10 males) were enrolled in the study. All of these individuals completed the study' (Participants). The 12/15 abstinence figure is computed over this full enrolled/completed sample, so N=15.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Comparator is Y because its absence is explicitly stated ('this pilot study was conducted without a control condition as a first step...'), which per the prompt counts as described. Blinding is Y because the open-label design is explicitly named throughout (title, Abstract 'we conducted an open-label pilot study', Discussion 'the open-label design does not allow for definitive conclusions'). Randomization is N because no statement anywhere addresses randomization (or its absence) for this study's own design - the text only discusses other trials' 'randomized controlled trials' and calls for a future 'randomized trial'. Sample_size_power is N because no power calculation (a priori or post hoc) or 'underpowered' language appears; the closest statement ('Results should be interpreted with caution given the small N and open-label design') addresses generalizability broadly, not power specifically. n_met=12 (one below the 13 threshold), so the binary is 0.

article.BaseStatus: FTCD (Fagerstrom Test for Cigarette Dependence) mean 5.3 (SD 1.3, range 3-8) on a 0-10 scale (Table 1); a mid-range mean conventionally denotes moderate nicotine dependence, and the sample also had heavy, long-standing use (mean 19 cigarettes/day for 31 years, mean 6 prior failed quit attempts) - coded 'Moderate'.
article.Age_Median: Mean age 51 (SD 10.5, range 26-65; Table 1) falls in the '50+' bracket.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Conducted at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA (author affiliations; IRB approval statement) - coded 'US'.
article.MediatingYN: The Discussion narratively proposes candidate psychological mechanisms (increased temporal horizon, self-efficacy, altered life priorities; Table 5 self-report mechanism endorsements) but no formal mediation model, indirect-effect test, or Baron-and-Kenny-style regression was run. Coded 0 per the field's requirement of a formal test, not narrative discussion.
article.ModeratingYN: No interaction term or formal moderation/subgroup-by-dose statistical test was reported. The article notes descriptively that 'the study design was unable to discern differential benefits of moderate dose and high dose sessions' and that all who quit did so after the initial moderate-dose session, but this is a narrative observation, not a tested interaction. Coded 0.
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: No inferential test (p-value, CI excluding null, or named test statistic) is reported for the primary Outcome value itself (the single-arm 80% abstinence rate has no comparator against which to test it). The article's hypothesis tests (paired t-tests, ANOVAs) apply to continuous secondary/supporting measures (TLFB counts, biomarkers, questionnaire scores), not to the abstinence-rate Outcome. Coded 0.
article.Implementation Outcome: Borderline call. The Abstract frames the study aim as 'to determine the safety and feasibility ... of psilocybin as an adjunct to tobacco smoking cessation treatment,' and Discussion states 'results of the present pilot study also support the feasibility of the approach.' However, the Abstract itself glosses feasibility as '(i.e., potential efficacy)', and the feasibility claim is operationalized entirely through the efficacy-style 80% abstinence rate rather than through classic implementation constructs (acceptability ratings, protocol fidelity, adoption, reach) measured with a dedicated instrument. Retention (15/15 completed) and two participants declining a third session are the closest process data but are not framed or analyzed as implementation outcomes. Coded 0; a reader weighting the explicit 'feasibility' aim language more heavily could reasonably code 1.
article.RelapseMeasured: Explicitly tracked and operationally defined: footnote 1 distinguishes 'lapses' (any smoking, even a puff, post-TQD) from 'relapses' (smoking on >=7 consecutive days post-TQD, per Hughes et al. 2003). Results report three participants' self-corrected lapses (1, 4, and 48 cigarettes) and one participant's relapse after 13 weeks of abstinence (average 5 cigarettes/day for 14 weeks) who resumed abstinence before 6-month follow-up. Coded 1.
article.Power: No power calculation (a priori or post hoc) or explicit 'underpowered' language appears anywhere; the caution statement about 'small N and open-label design' addresses sample size/generalizability broadly rather than statistical power specifically, so it does not meet the rule's 'bare statement study was underpowered' bar. Coded 0.
article.CulturalFraming: Discussion notes 'the relative racial homogeneity ... of the present study sample' as a limitation on generalizability, but this is a demographic/sampling observation, not an explicit engagement with racial/ethnic identity, historical trauma, or culturally specific language/context as intervention content. Coded 0.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded '.' because the article never reports a single consolidated count of participants with >=1 AE across the three AE categories (6/15 challenging experience, 8/10 headache, an unquantified subset with cardiovascular changes) - summing the per-type counts would risk double-counting participants with more than one AE type, so no aggregate is fabricated.
article.AE_denominator: AE data are assessed over two different denominators depending on type: the full N=15 psilocybin-exposed sample for cardiovascular changes and challenging-experience ratings (assessed across all 42 sessions in all 15 participants), versus a 10-participant subset for headache - the Post-session Headache Interview was added only after the first 5 participants had already completed their sessions ('The first five participants had completed their psilocybin sessions when another study found that psilocybin increased headache occurrence... Therefore, the final ten participants completed a staff-administered scale'). AE_denominator is coded 15 as the primary safety population; the headache-specific subset (n=10, 8 affected) is captured in that AE's own Description/NAffected instead.
article.SchemaRevisionNote: 2026-09-03 schema-revision splice: ConfoundYN/PVal removed, MediatingYN/ModeratingYN/HypothesisTestReportedYN added, sourced from a separate v3 extraction run (PromptVersion v1.3) rather than this file's own v1.2 run. ae_events.Johnson 2014_AE01: Results (Safety data): 'one participant (7%) reported extreme ratings, and five others (33%) reported strong ratings of fear, fear of insanity, or feeling trapped at some time during a session. These episodes occurred in six participants (40%)... They were readily managed by interpersonal support, and had resolved by the end of the sessions.' Coded AE_type='challenging_experience' per the prompt's guidance that CEQ-sense in-session phenomenology should be flagged rather than counted as a clinical AE. Onset='in-session' because it resolved by end of session. Severity='Mild'/SeveritySource='rubric' because the rubric explicitly treats a high CEQ score as Mild absent intervention need or persistence, both absent here. InterventionRequired='N' because management was purely interpersonal support, not pharmacological rescue (rescue medication was available per protocol but the text states no clinically significant AE required physician or pharmacologic intervention).
ae_events.Johnson 2014_AE02: Results (Safety data): 'blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) were elevated during drug effects with peak values occurring on average between 1.5 and 2.5 hours post-psilocybin administration' with group mean peak/baseline values given for systolic BP, diastolic BP, and HR. Grouped as one AE type ('acute cardiovascular changes') rather than split into separate BP/HR entries because the article always reports and discusses them together as one physiological phenomenon; Discussion explicitly lists 'modest acute increases in blood pressure, heart rate' among 'adverse effects associated with psilocybin.' NAffected is coded '.' because only session-level group means (SD, range) are given, not a count of participants affected. Severity='Mild' matches the rubric's own example ('transient mild BP/HR elevation'); SeveritySource='rubric' since no CTCAE grade or SAE label is assigned by the authors. InterventionRequired='N' per the blanket statement that no clinically significant AE required physician or pharmacologic intervention.
ae_events.Johnson 2014_AE03: Results (Safety data): 'Of the ten participants assessed for headache, eight reported at least one post-psilocybin headache with a mean (SD; range) duration of 5.8 (2.4; 2.0-9.5) hours, onset at a mean of 6.2 (2.1; 3.5-11.5) hours after psilocybin administration and mean severity rating of mild, or 2.6 (1.3; 1-5) on a scale from 1=minimal, to 6=excruciating. Five reported use of over-thecounter headache medication.' SeveritySource='author' because the authors themselves characterize the mean rating as 'mild' using their own study-specific severity scale, rather than the extractor applying the rubric de novo. Onset='post-session-acute' (hours after dosing, resolving within about a day) rather than 'in-session' or 'delayed'. InterventionRequired='N': the OTC medication was self-administered by participants after the monitored session window to alleviate symptoms ('approved medications for use during the study'), not a study-administered pharmacologic rescue, and is consistent with the blanket statement that no AE required physician or pharmacologic intervention.

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, open-label pilot with no control group; the study's headline SUD outcome (80% biologically verified abstinence, selected per abstract-leads-with precedence) is a raw proportion with no accompanying test statistic or comparator, so none of the seven supported conversions (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR) apply. The paired t-tests reported for continuous smoking/biomarker measures (t14=11.1 TLFB, t14=3.8 CO, t14=2.3 cotinine) are within-sample pre/post contrasts on the same single arm, not treatment-vs-control effects, and are deliberately not repurposed as a Tier-1 conversion input.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 80% (12/15) biologically verified 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence at 6-month follow-up in an open-label, single-arm pilot with no control group, substantially exceeding the <35% typical 6-month abstinence rate for standard smoking-cessation pharmacotherapies/behavioral treatments cited in the article's own Introduction and Discussion.
